clip35.title: Opened with ₹10 lakh. Ended at ₹453 crore. How? #Shorts
clip35.description:
Hanuman Ansh (released 7 Aug 2026) opened with about ₹10 lakh net in India, made ₹1.08 cr in week 1 and was down to 29 shows at the start of week 2. Then word of mouth: ₹61 cr in week 4 and ₹90.25 cr in week 5, over 80x its first week. Sacnilk's estimate after 110 days: ₹343 cr India net, ₹453 cr worldwide gross. Figures are trade estimates.

Sources:

clip36.title: Biologists believed this since 1972. A new study says it's wrong #Shorts
clip36.description:
A 1972 idea says organisms protect their most important genes by letting them mutate less. A University of Bath study in PLOS Biology tested it on what the authors call the largest collection of spontaneous mutations so far, in E. coli and baker's yeast: essential genes did not mutate less. Older results may come from 'ghost mutations', harmful mutations removed by selection before they're counted. Caveat: two microbes only.

Sources:
- ScienceDaily / University of Bath, 21 Nov 2026: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261119194538.htm
- Paper: Radrizzani & Hurst, PLOS Biology 2026, DOI 10.1371/journal.pbio.3004089
